receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI has signed a contract with Oracle to buy $300 billion worth of computing power over the next five years, according to the Wall Street Journal.

evidence_items.explanation: The same article says the contract begins in 2027, so most payments fall due after the post. Whether OpenAI can afford them is largely a future question.

evidence_items.explanation: Around the post date OpenAI had about $110B (later $122B) in committed funding. That counts against near-term inability to pay, though the same article says it was still burning cash and unprofitable.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI raised $122bn in March at an $852bn valuation, and the FT reports it is on track to exhaust that by 2028. The projection period runs two years beyond the money.

evidence_items.explanation: Projections show OpenAI would need more financing before 2028 to cover its compute plans. This supports his concern about future affordability, but it is a projection, not a missed payment.
